name: Ahmed Rajib Haider
role: Blogger, Shahbag activist, and assassination victim
contribution: Ahmed Rajib Haider was a blogger and activist associated with the 2013 Shahbag protests. His killing on 15 February 2013 intensified public attention to the movement and to threats against secular and civic voices.
context: His death occurred during the Shahbag mobilization over war-crimes accountability, amid counter-mobilization, ideological conflict, and rising security concerns. The killing and subsequent trial became part of a wider debate over extremism, speech, and due process.
impact: Haider became a symbol in competing public narratives about secular activism and political violence in Bangladesh. This profile records his activism and killing without treating symbolic status or later allegations as a substitute for judicial findings.
highlight: Blogger and Shahbag activist whose 2013 killing intensified debate over secular speech and political violence.
seoDescription: Learn about Ahmed Rajib Haider, the blogger and Shahbag activist whose 2013 killing became a major moment in Bangladesh's debate over extremism and civic freedom.
shortAnswer: Ahmed Rajib Haider was a blogger and Shahbag activist killed in February 2013 during a period of intense political and ideological conflict.

faq.question: Who was Ahmed Rajib Haider?
faq.answer: He was a blogger and activist associated with the 2013 Shahbag protests who was killed on 15 February 2013.

faq.question: Why is Rajib Haider remembered in the Shahbag context?
faq.answer: His killing intensified public attention to threats against secular and civic voices and became part of the movement's contested political memory.
